name: Himadri Speciality Chemical Ltd
title: Himadri Speciality Chemical Ltd - 500184 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Q1FY27 consolidated revenue INR1,432 Cr (+28% YoY) and EBITDA margin 22%, but the call is heavy on new capex (~INR2,000 Cr) and LFP/anode plans with no disclosed margins, and utilisation is 80% with management guiding to 90%+.

summary.headline: Himadri Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 28% to INR1,432 Crores, with PAT up 27% to INR228 Crores at a 16% margin.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 28% YoY to INR1,432 Crores, EBITDA rose 33% to INR313 Crores (22% margin), and PAT reached INR228 Crores. Standalone EBITDA grew 29% to INR301 Crores at a 24% margin. Management announced an indigenous CNT plant (200 MTPA, about INR70 Crores capex) and a super speciality carbon black conversion (6,000 MTPA, INR170 Crores capex), and reported that the 200 MTPA anode plant was commissioned in April 2026. Other-segment EBIT fell to about INR1 Crore from about INR25 Crores because mining did not operate pending licences, and an FX loss weighed on the quarter.

financial_highlights.change: Down from about INR25 Crores in the prior quarter, due to no mining income

segments.name: Birla Tyres
segments.commentary: Commercial operations began 29 May 2025; quarterly revenue is cited at about INR127 Crores and is consolidated but not in standalone. Management targets INR3,000 Crores top line in 4-5 years and EBITDA breakeven in FY27, with a PCR plant by FY28. Distribution spans 49 distributors and over 1,000 dealers.

segments.name: Coal tar and carbon black (core)
segments.commentary: Holds over 65% domestic coal tar pitch share with 600,000 MTPA distillation capacity, and carbon black capacity is 250,000 MT including 130,000 MT speciality grades. Anthraquinone and carbazole capacity of 5,300 MTPA is due in two phases: 2,600 MTPA in Q2 FY27 and 2,700 MTPA in Q2 FY28.

segments.name: New energy materials
segments.commentary: A 200 MTPA anode plant at Mahistikry was commissioned in April 2026, with anode capex of about INR120 Crores to date. LFP cathode initial 2,000 MTPA is due in Q3 FY27 as Phase 1 of a 40,000 MTPA expansion (about INR1,125 Crores) that is due in FY28.

segments.name: Other (mining)
segments.commentary: No mining operations in Q1 as environmental and licensing approvals are awaited, with timing of 3 to 6 months cited. Segment EBIT fell to about INR1 Crore from about INR25 Crores.

guidance_outlook: Management maintained the INR1,100 Crores PAT target for FY28 and said nothing had changed, but gave no FY27 guidance.

Total capex announced is about INR2,000 Crores (LFP INR1,125 Crores, new announcements INR368 Crores, Birla Tyres INR500 Crores this year), with about INR1,000 Crores expected in each of FY27 and FY28.
Management said free cash flow will fund the capex with no incremental debt.
Management expects top-line growth from both volume and value next quarter.
Birla Tyres is expected to reach EBITDA breakeven and be cash positive in FY27.
Management said 40,000 MTPA LFP would yield about INR3,000 Crores top line at current prices, and 200,000 MTPA LFP would need about INR4,800 Crores capex.
capex_capacity: CNT: 200 MTPA plant, about INR70 Crores capex, commissioning targeted for Q4 FY27.
Super speciality carbon black: conversion of 6,000 MTPA existing capacity for INR170 Crores, with capacity start in FY28.
Anode: 200 MTPA plant commissioned April 2026, with no further anode capex announced; natural graphite and silicon carbon capacity planned.
LFP cathode: 2,000 MTPA initial capacity in Q3 FY27, Phase 1 of 40,000 MTPA in FY28, long-term target 200,000 MTPA in 5-6 years.
Anthraquinone and carbazole: 2,600 MTPA in Q2 FY27 and 2,700 MTPA in Q2 FY28; India's first commercial plant of its kind.
IBC plans a 7 GW battery facility in India, with operations expected by Q4 FY27, which will use Himadri raw material.
demand_pricing: Management cited global Li-ion battery demand rising from about 1.6 TWh in 2025 to about 6.8 TWh by 2035, with about 70% of growth in LFP.
CNT global market is about 30,000 MT; super speciality carbon black market is about 300,000 MT; speciality is over 1 million MT.
LFP pricing is said to be at parity with China, and management claims a cost advantage from India-based production and non-China raw materials.
Anode qualification: sample B supplied to customers; sample process takes 1.5-2 years, and management says approvals will be in place by commissioning.
Management says the West Asia situation did not materially affect supply; raw-material cost pass-through lifted finished-product prices.
Other expenses fell to about INR148 Crores excluding forex loss, from about INR172 Crores in Q4, driven by lower outbound freight and cost optimisation.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other-segment EBIT drop from INR25 Crores to about INR1 Crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Mining did not operate this quarter while licences are awaited, so the mining profit did not recur; higher Birla Tyres revenue offset top-line effects.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue potential of the new capex?
qa_highlights.answer: 40,000 MTPA LFP at today's prices gives about INR3,000 Crores top line; anthraquinone/carbazole about INR250-300 Crores; super speciality carbon black about 3x capex (about INR500 Crores); CNT less than INR100 Crores; 200 MTPA anode about INR120-130 Crores.

qa_highlights.question: Is the FX loss a recurring issue and what drove other income?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there was no hedging policy change and the FX loss was a one-off for the currency volatility; other income came from FD and mutual fund deployment, borrowings in CPs and mark-to-market gains on IBC, Sicona and Birla Tyres NCDs, and may swing 30-40% QoQ.

qa_highlights.question: Will the LFP and new capex be debt-funded?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said free cash flow will cover the capex with no incremental debt.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company increase its stake in IBC?
qa_highlights.answer: No; management called IBC a strategic investment and said it is not looking to raise its stake further.

qa_highlights.question: What are the margins on the new CNT and SSCB products?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to disclose margins, saying they are significantly higher than existing speciality carbon black.

qa_highlights.question: Is the LFP cathode economics viable against Chinese pricing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Excel-based cost comparisons are not reliable, cited cost advantages, and declined to disclose lithium carbonate sourcing.

risks_watch: Mining remains idle pending environmental clearance, which could take 3-6 months, with segment EBIT near zero.
Execution on LFP (2,000 MTPA in Q3 FY27, 40,000 MTPA in FY28) and anode commercialisation depends on customer approvals, which management said take 1.5-2 years.
Birla Tyres is not yet EBITDA positive, and its breakeven is targeted within FY27 after the TBB to OTR conversion.
Analysts questioned whether LFP pricing at China parity leaves a positive gross spread; management declined to disclose input costs.
Other income is volatile (30-40% QoQ swing) and the FX loss needs to be watched next quarter.
summary.management_tone: Confident and expansive on long-term growth and new products, but evasive on specifics: margins, lithium sourcing, customer timelines and FY27 guidance were withheld, with 'competitive nature' cited for limited disclosure.
key_quotes: Our Coal Tar Pitch business continues to anchor the company.
We don't give quarter and year guidelines, never.
There's no more capex we have announced now.
There is no question of any incremental debt.

2,000 MTPA LFP cathode initial capacity (Phase 1 of 40,000 MTPA expansion)
6,000 MTPA super speciality carbon black conversion of existing capacity

growth.why: No FY27 revenue guidance; FY28 PAT target of INR1,100 Cr held, with management expecting volume and value top-line growth next quarter, backed by commissioned anode plant, 2,600 MTPA anthraquinone/carbazole due Q2 FY27, LFP cathode 2,000 MTPA due Q3 FY27 and utilisation rising from 80% to 90%+, though order-level contracts were not quantified.
